Lazebnik--Lundberg prove an extremal example with exactly \(3n-1\) zeros, verify that the associated harmonic function has no singular zeros, and in Remark 3.5 already record openness under variation of the construction parameter \(c\). Their paper also quotes the prior universal \(3n-1\) upper bound. Once every base zero is nonsingular, the real-analytic implicit-function theorem applied to the full finite coefficient vector gives \(3n-1\) persistent distinct branches; the existing global upper bound prevents extra roots. The orientation split persists by continuity of the nonzero Jacobian. Thus the audited theorem is implication-covered even though the exact phrase “all coefficients” is not printed in the source.
